title: Security Command Center

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `google:gcp:pubsub:message` events with `resource.type="scc_finding"` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.3.5 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `google:gcp:pubsub:message` traffic without `resource.type="scc_finding"`. Confirm UC-4.3.5 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="scc_finding"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.5_security_command_center_5"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.3.5 — Security Command Center: queries Google Cloud `google:gcp:pubsub:message` for search criteria `resource.type="scc_finding"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, detecting 'Security Command Center' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.3.5 drives critical-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure SCC to publish findings to Pub/Sub. Ingest via Splunk TA. Alert on CRITICAL and HIGH severity findings.
visualization: Table by severity, Bar chart (finding categories), Trend line.
knownFalsePositives: A fresh scanner run or a vendor re-rate can resurface a finding we already know about. We deduplicate on resource and time and we only escalate when the exposure is new or the severity stepped up.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure SCC to publish findings to Pub/Sub. Ingest via Splunk TA. Alert on CRITICAL and HIGH severity findings.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="scc_finding"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.5_security_command_center_5"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect security command center. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_5_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table by severity, Bar chart (finding categories), Trend line..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of security command center so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
